chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār wrote to Abī Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: “What is the prescribed limit of the water with which the deceased is washed, just as they have narrated that the junub performs ghusl with six ratls of water and the menstruating woman with nine ratls? Is there for the deceased a prescribed limit of the water with which he is washed?”
So he عليه السلام wrote in reply: “The limit of the ghusl of the deceased is that he is washed until he becomes pure, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.”

key_terms.الْجُنُبَ: a person in a state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person to be washed

ai.seo_question: Is there a fixed amount of water required for ghusl of the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question to Imam al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام about whether washing the deceased has a fixed prescribed quantity of water. The Imam’s reply indicates that the criterion is not a fixed measure, but washing until purification is achieved, by the will of Allah the Exalted.
